items.title: Real matrix Laplace tail

source.label: Tropp, matrix Laplace transform tail bound

items.statement: Let X be a self-adjoint random matrix on a probability space. For every real threshold t, its largest-eigenvalue upper-tail probability is bounded by infimum over positive s of exp(−st) times the expected unnormalized trace of exp(sX). The selected formal version restricts to finite nonempty real matrices, makes almost-sure measurability/self-adjointness explicit, and permits a nonnegative scalar extended expectation as a disclosed domain completion. Tropp §3.1 notes that the matrix MGF need not exist for every parameter; the completion does not claim that all matrix MGFs are finite.
assumptions: Let \((\Omega,\Sigma,\mu)\) be a probability space, let \(\mathcal I\) be finite and nonempty, and let \(X:\Omega\to\operatorname{Mat}_{\mathcal I}(\mathbb R)\) be almost-everywhere strongly measurable and self-adjoint almost everywhere. The threshold \(t\) is any real number.

\(\lambda_{\max}\) denotes the algebraically largest real eigenvalue on the self-adjoint domain; it is not the operator norm. The trace is the ordinary unnormalized trace, and \(e^A\) is the matrix-algebra power-series exponential.

The bar on \(\overline{\mathbb E}\) means a nonnegative scalar integral, permitted to be \(+\infty\). The real coefficient \(e^{-st}\) is finite and strictly positive for every \(s>0\). This is an explicit domain completion of the source inequality, not a claim that the source defines ENNReal or that every matrix MGF exists as a Bochner integral.

Neither centering, independence, a norm cap nor a variance bound is a premise of the public theorem. Almost-everywhere event comparison handles the null exceptional self-adjoint set; no separate eigenbasis selector or general eigenvalue measurability theorem is claimed.

obligations.label: The real largest-eigenvalue trace-exponential tail reduction, with the disclosed scalar extended-expectation completion.

bindings.boundary: This packet proves the real extended-expectation Laplace-tail reduction and its private finite-Bochner-expectation application to all four literal signed Gaussian sums. It does not bound their trace MGF, prove Lieb/independent-sum master-tail or Bernstein, close C6/Lemma4.4 or either main lower bound, or supply the strict-norm union bridge, oracle/TV/precision/query-cap/expected-cost adapters. Main/site/global graph integration, purification and whole-Goal acceptance remain separate.

assumption_deltas.source: A self-adjoint random matrix; ordinary trace and largest algebraic eigenvalue.
assumption_deltas.lean: Finite nonempty real matrices; AE Hermitian; sSup of the real spectrum; ordinary Matrix.trace and matrix-algebra exponential.
assumption_deltas.reason: Explicit real specialization. The largest eigenvalue is not replaced by the operator norm and no dimension factor is silently normalized away.

assumption_deltas.source: Probability and §2.2 standing regularity, with random-matrix relations understood almost surely.
assumption_deltas.lean: IsProbabilityMeasure μ, AEStronglyMeasurable X μ and AE Hermiticity.
assumption_deltas.reason: Continuity supplies measurable trace exponentials, and measure_mono_ae transfers the source-domain event comparison. No eigenbasis selector premise is added.

assumption_deltas.source: Prop3.1 expectation bound; §3.1 warns that some positive parameters can lack a matrix MGF.
assumption_deltas.lean: A nonnegative scalar lintegral valued in ENNReal; no generic Bochner-integrability premise.
assumption_deltas.reason: Disclosed extended-expectation domain completion, proved by nonnegative Markov. Infinite scalar expectations remain legitimate terms. This is not extended matrix-valued expectation or a statement that every source MGF exists.

assumption_deltas.source: Every real t and infimum over positive real parameters.
assumption_deltas.lean: t : ℝ and an iInf over {s : ℝ // 0<s}.
assumption_deltas.reason: No positivity condition on the threshold, no negative-parameter or lower-tail identification, and no minimizer-existence requirement.
